answer.rationale: Finance's 18% mandate is the binding constraint. memory_c2 reports that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year, with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, and that vendor's current quote already meets the mandate. memory_c5's pattern of month-to-month continuation provides the hedge for the incumbent's 14-day expiry: we keep the incumbent on short-term month-to-month terms to preserve delivery coverage during the switch, mitigating risk at 94% line utilization with no buffer. This satisfies the mandate now without increasing delivery risk if the incumbent bridge holds. I verify c2 first because it is the only memory that directly supports switching, and the archived record is the one I am about to lean on hardest.
